phase_name: HATP Trust-Enrollment Implementation Capability Independent Verification
phase_title: HATP Trust-Enrollment Implementation Capability Independent Verification
recommended_next_phase: 149O.20L.7O.2F.2 -- FIDO2 Signing-Time Credential Resolution Repair. Must begin with an explicit contract-level decision between authenticator rediscovery and durable-registry signer resolution before any repair implementation. Not performed by this phase.
summary: Independently verified Phase 149O.20L.7O.2F's HATP Trust-Enrollment Implementation Capability against HPSE-001 v1.1, HHCE-001 v1.1, and the already-frozen HSCE-001 signing-ceremony contract, in an isolated git worktree. Surfaces B, C, D, and E independently re-verified clean: HHCE-001 writer idempotency/conflict/lock/revocation discipline, the continuous two-lock cross-registry critical section (closing NBF-1), PrincipalRecord.revoked_at schema widening (Surface D), and the DeploymentBinding producer's cross-registry validation (Surface E) were each re-derived from primary source, not accepted from 2F's own report. Surface A's enroll_credential() is well-built in isolation but the capability is Blocking at the system level: hatp_signing_ceremony.py::_resolve_signer, the sole identity-resolution path for the real pcae hatp sign rollback command under the already-frozen HSCE-001 contract, calls provider.credential_identity() unconditionally, and Fido2HardwareProvider.credential_identity() remains an unconditional raise, unchanged by 2F (BF-1). Independently, enroll_credential()'s CTAP2 makeCredential call omits the resident-key option, minting a non-resident credential incompatible with credential_identity()'s own resident/discoverable credential model (BF-2) -- a second, independent gap, not merely a consequence of BF-1. Neither gap was disclosed in 2F's own report. The regression delta was independently re-derived (not inherited from 2F's 304-node deselection set) by diffing two environments -- with and without the fido2 package installed -- against the actual phase-entry commit (d11b8cd0) via git worktree, not git stash: 11 net-new failing node IDs in both environments, each individually confirmed (two spot-checked directly) as the expected byte-identity/no-new-production-module self-check family tripped because 2F legitimately touched the files its own phase doc claims, not an undisclosed trust-boundary regression. 2F's own claimed 46+54 passing Surface A/B/C tests were independently re-run (not accepted) with real fido2 installed: 100/100 passed. Overall verdict: BLOCKED. No repair attempted this phase; recommends 149O.20L.7O.2F.2 (FIDO2 Signing-Time Credential Resolution Repair), beginning with an explicit contract-level decision between authenticator rediscovery and durable-registry signer resolution.

validation_results.name: credential_identity_vs_enroll_credential_architectural_correctness
validation_results.result: Independently re-derived from hatp_signing_ceremony.py::_resolve_signer, Fido2HardwareProvider, SignerRecord, and HSCE-001: Answer B, not A. _resolve_signer (the sole identity-resolution path for production_sign_rollback_evidence, the real pcae hatp sign rollback command) calls provider.credential_identity() unconditionally at hatp_fido2_provider.py-consuming line 542; Fido2HardwareProvider.credential_identity() remains an unconditional raise at hatp_fido2_provider.py:307-313, unchanged by 2F. No FIDO2 signer enrolled via this phase's Surfaces A-E can ever sign real evidence in production.

validation_results.name: enroll_credential_non_resident_credential_incompatibility
validation_results.result: enroll_credential()'s ctap2.make_credential(...) call (hatp_fido2_provider.py:361-367) passes no options map, so the CTAP2 rk bit defaults to false -- the minted credential is non-resident. credential_identity()'s own error text requires a resident/discoverable credential. A future credential_identity() built on resident-credential discovery could not find a credential Surface A itself mints -- independent of BF-1.
